case_name: Heera Lal vs State Of Rajasthan

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Rajasthan, Superintendent Of Police, Rajsamand, Station House Officer, Police Station Devgarh, District Rajsamand

facts_of_case: Petitioners' minor sons and daughters are missing since January 31, 2022. Petitions allege that police are not making sincere efforts to trace out the minors.

legal_principles.principle: The court's primary concern is the welfare of the child.
legal_principles.held: Though, as per the school record, the age of the corpus 'K' is around 16 years and 2 months as of today, but to ascertain her level of maturity and intelligence, we have asked many questions to her in open Court in the presence of her parents and the advocates and we have found that she is mature and intelligent enough to take her own decisions.

legal_principles.principle: The court should consider the best interests of the child when making decisions.
legal_principles.held: We have interacted with the corpus Ramesh and corpus 'K' and both of them have stated that they left their house as per their own free will and have solemnized marriage. The corpus 'K' is carrying a daughter aged one year and one month and both of them have stated that the said daughter is born out of their wedlock.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not make decisions that would lead to uncertainty or harm to the child.
legal_principles.held: If we handover the custody of corpus 'K' to her parents, there is all possibility that the parents of the corpus 'K' may marry her to some other person in the due course of time and in such circumstances, the future of one year old daughter of the corpus 'K' would be uncertain.

outcome.final_order: Police traced out the minor children and produced them before this Court on July 13, 2023.
